what: Option 2: construct a TE annotation object manually
title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: Users may also construct required GRanges object RepeatMasker-style BED table. resulting object standard GRanges object TE metadata columns Harmonize chromosome naming check object
code: library(GenomicRanges) library(IRanges)  te_table <- read.delim(   "repeats_mm10.bed",   header = TRUE,   sep = "\t",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) te_table <- te_table[   grep("(DNA)|(LINE)|(LTR)|(SINE)", te_table$repClass, perl = TRUE), ] te <- GRanges(   seqnames = te_table$genoName,   ranges = IRanges(     start = te_table$genoStart,     end = te_table$genoEnd   ),   strand = te_table$strand,   names = te_table$repName,   class = te_table$repClass,   family = te_table$repFamily ) te <- NCBI_check(te) saveRDS(   te,   file = te_file )

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: TEDDY uses StringTie perform per-sample, reference-guided transcript assembly aligned short-read RNA-seq BAM files, enabling local reconstruction novel isoform structures. long-read data, ONT PacBio RNA-seq, use per-sample workflow set longRead = TRUE: Notes params argument passes additional options StringTie. example , params = "-p 8" allocates 8 threads sample-level assembly. Several StringTie parameters particularly relevant TE-chimeric transcript reconstruction: -j: minimum junction coverage. Increasing threshold makes splice-junction evidence stringent, may remove low-coverage TE-chimeric junctions. -c: minimum read coverage assembled transcripts. Higher values reduce weakly supported transcript fragments may also remove low-abundance isoforms. -s: minimum coverage single-exon transcripts. useful controlling weak single-exon fragments. -f: minimum isoform fraction. Higher values retain relatively abundant isoforms within locus, whereas lower values permissive minor isoforms. -: minimum anchor length junctions. helps filter splice junctions supported short anchors. -m: minimum assembled transcript length. removes short transcript fragments. -M: maximum fraction bundle allowed covered multi-mapping reads. can useful repeat-rich regions, including TE-associated loci. Users can adjust parameters params according sequencing depth, library complexity, desired balance sensitivity specificity. example:
code: bamfiles <- list.files(   bam_dir,   pattern = "\\.bam$",   full.names = TRUE )  mclapply(   bamfiles,   FUN = function(x, reference, outdir) {     bam <- basename(x)     outfile <- file.path(outdir, sub("\\.bam$", ".gtf", bam))     Teddy::stringtieAssembly(       bam = x,       reference = reference,       outfile = outfile,       params = "-p 8"     )   },   reference = reference,   outdir = file.path(work_dir, "gtf"),   mc.cores = 8 ) bamfiles <- list.files(   bam_dir,   pattern = "\\.bam$",   full.names = TRUE )  mclapply(   bamfiles,   FUN = function(x, reference, outdir) {     bam <- basename(x)     outfile <- file.path(outdir, sub("\\.bam$", ".gtf", bam))     Teddy::stringtieAssembly(       bam = x,       reference = reference,       outfile = outfile,       params = "-p 8",       longRead = TRUE     )   },   reference = reference,   outdir = file.path(work_dir, "gtf"),   mc.cores = 4 ) Teddy::stringtieAssembly(   bam = "sample.bam",   reference = reference,   outfile = "sample.gtf",   params = "-p 8 -j 2 -c 1 -f 0.01" )

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: per-sample reconstruction, TEDDY uses stringtieMerge() combine assembled GTF files. step harmonizes transcript isoforms across samples reduces redundant transcript structures. merged GTF file written : Notes params argument passes additional options StringTie merge mode. example , params = "-p 8" uses 8 threads. TE-chimeric transcript analysis, following merge-mode parameters particularly relevant: -m: minimum input transcript length include merge. StringTie default 50. -c: minimum input transcript coverage include merge. StringTie default 0. -F -T: minimum FPKM TPM thresholds input transcripts. StringTie defaults 1.0 . Lowering thresholds can retain low-abundance transcript models downstream TE-chimeric inspection. -f: minimum isoform fraction. StringTie default 0.01. -g: maximum gap transcripts merge together. StringTie default 250. Users can adjust thresholds according sequencing depth, library complexity, expected abundance TE-chimeric isoforms. permissive settings may help retain low-abundance TE-associated structures, whereas stringent settings reduce weakly supported transcript fragments. example uses permissive merge setting lowering FPKM TPM thresholds 0. may useful retaining low-abundance TE-chimeric candidates, users may choose stringent thresholds noisy datasets.
code: gtffiles <- list.files(   file.path(work_dir, "gtf"),   pattern = "\\.gtf$",   full.names = TRUE )  stringtieMerge(   reference = reference,   gtfFiles = gtffiles,   outfile = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "merged.gtf"),   params = "-p 8" ) short_read_teddy_output/GTF/merged.gtf stringtieMerge(   reference = reference,   gtfFiles = gtffiles,   outfile = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "merged.gtf"),   params = "-p 8 -m 50 -c 0 -F 0 -T 0" )

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: TEDDY uses gffcompareAnno() compare merged transcriptome reference input reference GTF. step assigns transcript class-code information generates standardized annotated GTF. annotated GTF file written :
code: gffcompareAnno(   reference = reference,   gtffile = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "merged.gtf"),   outfile = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "annotated.gtf"),   overwrite = TRUE ) short_read_teddy_output/GTF/Teddy.annotated.gtf

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: TEDDY uses prepareAnno() convert annotated transcript GTF exon-level transcript features annotate TE-chimeric exons. output GRanges object range represents exonic part associated transcript, gene, exon-rank, TE-overlap information. Example output: Notes tx_id tx_name store transcript identifiers. gene_id stores corresponding gene locus. exon_rank records exon position within transcript exon chain strand-aware order. exonic_part indexes flattened exonic segment within corresponding gene locus strand-aware order. transposon stores associated TE name TE-chimeric exons.

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: TEDDY uses stringtieCombine() re-quantify annotated unified transcriptome GTF across BAM files. output RangedSummarizedExperiment object stores transcript-level expression matrices corresponding transcript structure annotation. long-read data, use annotated unified GTF set longRead = TRUE:
code: combineSE <- stringtieCombine(   reference = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "annotated.gtf"),   params = "-p 8",   gtfFiles = gtffiles,   bamFiles = bamfiles,   longRead = FALSE,   cores = 4 ) combineSE_longread <- stringtieCombine(   reference = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "annotated.gtf"),   params = "-p 8",   gtfFiles = gtffiles,   bamFiles = bamfiles,   longRead = TRUE,   cores = 4 )

what: 8.2 Build a unified cross-platform transcriptome reference
title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: TEDDY uses stringtieMerge() merge platform-specific annotated GTF files unified cross-platform transcriptome reference. step consolidates transcript structures reconstructed different sequencing platforms.
code: cross_platform_gtf <- file.path(   work_dir,   "GTF",   "cross_platform_pool.gtf" )  stringtieMerge(   reference = reference,   gtfFiles = platform_gtfs,   outfile = cross_platform_gtf,   params = "-p 8" )

title: Tutorial for TEDDY Core Workflow
text: building unified cross-platform reference, TEDDY uses buildIsoformSupport() compare platform-specific GTF unified reference. resulting table records whether transcript structure exactly supported platform. Notes default, support defined exact structural concordance platform-specific transcript unified reference. FPKM matrix provided, threshold can used require transcript-level expression support addition structural concordance.
code: platform_support <- buildIsoformSupport(   reference = cross_platform_gtf,   gtffiles = platform_gtfs,   conditions = names(platform_gtfs),   out_dir = file.path(work_dir, "GTF", "cross_platform_compare"),   out_prefix = "platform",   cores = 4 )  saveRDS(   platform_support,   file = file.path(work_dir, "meta", "cross_platform_isoform_support.rds") )

title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis
text: TEDDY uses ChimericDrivenTest() test whether TE-chimeric exonic bins show condition-associated usage changes relative exonic bins gene locus.

title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis

text: calculateFoldchange() can used estimate TE-chimeric exon usage fold changes selected candidate genes. Notes candidate_genes can selected extractTest() results. crossVar match condition variable used ChimericDrivenTest(). returned object stores fold-change estimates selected TE-chimeric candidate loci.

what: 3.1 Prepare exon-level GTF input for visualization
title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis

Option 1: use annotated unified GTF generated core workflow Option 2: use annotated GTF stored combineSE Notes filter specifies minimum FPKM threshold used extracting transcript structures.
code: GTF <- extractGTF(   gtfFile = annotated_gtf,   filter = 1,   type = "exon" ) combineSE <- readRDS(combineSE_file)  GTF <- extractGTF(   combineSE = combineSE,   filter = 1,   type = "exon" )

what: 3.2 Visualize TE-chimeric transcript structure with formPlot()
title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis
text: formPlot() displays exon-chain structure selected transcript highlights associated TE-derived exon. Select candidate transcript TE feature chi_GTF: Generate transcript structure plot:  Notes rank indicates transcript-order rank TE-overlapping exon can obtained tx_exon_rank column chi_GTF.
code: chi_GTF <- readRDS(chi_GTF_file) txid <- chi_GTF$transcript_id[1] geneName <- chi_GTF$gene_name[1] TEname <- chi_GTF$TE_name[1] formPlot(   GTF = GTF,   txid = txid,   rank = 1,   geneName = geneName,   TEname = TEname )

what: 3.3 Visualize TE-associated bin-level expression with diffBinPlot()
title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis
text: diffBinPlot() visualizes bin-level expression patterns selected candidate locus together transcript structure TE-associated exon. Generate bin-level visualization:  Notes count_mat extracted bin-level SummarizedExperiment generated countAnno(). annotation bin-level annotation stored rowData(se). chi_test result extracted ChimericDrivenTest() shown Section 2.
code: se <- readRDS(se_file) anno <- readRDS(anno_file) target_gene <- chi_test$groupID[1] txid <- as.character(anno$tx_name[anno$gene_id == target_gene][[1]][1])   idx <- which(anno$gene_id == target_gene) target_gene_name <- mapGeneName(target_gene, GTF) count_mat <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se) condition <- c(   "control", "control", "control",   "treatment", "treatment", "treatment" ) labels <- c("control", "treatment")  diffBinPlot(   count = count_mat,   conditions = condition,   annotation = anno,   idx = idx,   labels = labels,   Title = target_gene_name,   gtf = GTF,   txid = txid,   chi_test = chi_test,   gene_name = target_gene_name )

title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis
text: illustration, use Nelfa example candidate gene. Notes Select gene interest. Candidate genes can chosen chi_GTF significant results chi_test.  compare relative isoform usage, set ratio = TRUE:  Notes group defines sample-level labels can derived colnames(combineSE) using helper function clean_sampleNames. ratio = FALSE plots transcript-level expression values; ratio = TRUE plots relative fraction selected isoforms within group.
code: combineSE <- readRDS(combineSE_file) chi_GTF <- readRDS(chi_GTF_file) te <- readRDS(te_file)  gene <- "Nelfa"  chimeric_tx <- pick_chimeric_tx(   gene = gene,   combineSE = combineSE,   te = te,   return_all = FALSE )  canonical_tx <- pick_canonical_tx(   combineSE = combineSE,   gene = gene,   assay_name = "FPKM" )  txid <- c(   TE_chimeric = chimeric_tx,   Canonical = canonical_tx )  txid <- txid[!is.na(txid)] group <- clean_sampleNames(colnames(combineSE)) group_order <- unique(group)  plotIsoformDynamics(   combineSE = combineSE,   txid = txid,   gene_name = gene,   assay_name = "FPKM",   group = group,   group_order = group_order,   ratio = FALSE,   cols = c(      "#de7b60",      "#3c415e"   ) ) plotIsoformDynamics(   combineSE = combineSE,   txid = txid,   gene_name = gene,   assay_name = "FPKM",   group = group,   group_order = group_order,   ratio = TRUE,   cols = c(       "#de7b60",       "#3c415e"    ) )

title: Tutorial for Downstream Analysis
text: export_transcript() extracts transcript sequences exon structures, either concatenating single spliced sequence (collapse = TRUE) returning exons separately (collapse = FALSE).
